                    ### Question
                    A healthy 31-year-old woman comes to the physician because she is trying to conceive. She is currently timing the frequency of intercourse with at-home ovulation test kits. An increase in the levels of which of the following is the best indicator that ovulation has occurred?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Estrogen
opb. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
opc. Follicle stimulating hormone
opd. Progesterone
ope. Luteinizing hormone
"

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The best indicator that ovulation has occurred is an increase in luteinizing hormone (LH) levels. The LH surge is a critical event that triggers ovulation, occurring shortly before the release of the egg. While estrogen levels rise as the follicle matures and progesterone levels increase post-ovulation due to the formation of the corpus luteum, these are not immediate indicators of ovulation. Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) play roles in the menstrual cycle but are not direct indicators of ovulation. Therefore, the most accurate and immediate marker of ovulation is the increase in luteinizing hormone.
